query: I work in the claims team. We want to cut the time our handlers spend reading and summarising new claim packs so they can help members faster. How should we build this?
context: Framework: gate the request, prefer the simplest useful technology, and recommend a cast of roles. Acme standards: read-only/draft work is low risk; any write-back to claims is human-approved (Consumer Duty); structured data lives in Guidewire + Azure Data Platform, unstructured in Microsoft 365/SharePoint, custom grounding via Azure AI Search; default to a single agent; stay in the Azure UK landing zone.
ground_truth: Recommend an assistive, read-only/draft claims-summarisation copilot (not an autonomous claims agent). Keep the handler in the loop; no autonomous write-back. Ground on Guidewire/Azure Data Platform (structured) and SharePoint via Azure AI Search (unstructured). Front door in the handler workflow or Copilot Studio; engine in Azure AI Foundry/Azure OpenAI. Single agent. Include an Architect Review noting UK boundary, action safety, approved platforms.
expected_platforms: Copilot Studio, Azure AI Search, Azure AI Foundry/Azure OpenAI, Guidewire, Azure Data Platform

query: When a policy is 30 days from expiry we want the system to automatically send the member a templated renewal reminder email. Should we build an AI agent for this?
context: Framework agent checkpoint: deterministic, rule-based, triggered tasks usually do NOT need an agent; prefer workflow/automation. Acme standards: low-code automation belongs in Power Platform; triggered automation needs defined triggers and observability.
ground_truth: Say this does not need an AI agent. It is a deterministic, trigger-based workflow: use Power Automate (Power Platform) with a templated email on a policy-expiry trigger. No LLM reasoning required. Note observability and ownership. Include Architect Review.

query: We want an AI that gives our customers personalised pension and investment advice automatically, end to end, with no adviser involved.
context: Acme standards: customer-facing financial advice is the highest-risk tier; Consumer Duty and FCA rules require explainability, audit, and human accountability; no autonomous advice or money-moving actions; human-in-the-loop mandatory. Framework: reshape scenarios that fail action-safety.
ground_truth: Do not recommend fully automated customer advice. Reshape to an adviser-assist copilot: the AI drafts/summarises and surfaces options, a regulated human adviser reviews and owns the advice (Consumer Duty, FCA). Mandatory human-in-the-loop, explainability, audit trail. Flag the regulatory blocker clearly. Include Architect Review.
expected_platforms: Adviser Hub, Azure AI Foundry/Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search

query: We want to help our office staff draft emails, summarise Teams meetings, and find documents faster. What should we use?
context: Framework: check Microsoft-managed end-user copilots before building anything custom. Acme standards: Microsoft-first; Microsoft 365 is the primary employee surface and Microsoft 365 Copilot is rolling out.
ground_truth: Recommend adopting Microsoft 365 Copilot (managed, grouping 1) rather than building anything custom. No agent build needed. Note licensing/rollout and that it works inside Teams/Outlook/SharePoint. Include Architect Review.

query: We want staff to ask questions and get answers grounded in our underwriting manuals, which live in SharePoint, ideally inside the tools they already use.
context: Framework: prefer extending an existing copilot before a custom build. Acme standards: unstructured knowledge lives in Microsoft 365/SharePoint reachable via Microsoft Graph; Microsoft 365 Copilot is the employee surface.
ground_truth: Recommend extending Microsoft 365 Copilot with the SharePoint underwriting content (grouping 2) via grounding/declarative agent or a Copilot Studio agent over SharePoint/Graph, rather than a bespoke app. Note security trimming and citations. Include Architect Review.
expected_platforms: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Graph/SharePoint

query: We want to analyse claims trends across the whole business and let our analysts ask questions of the data in natural language.
context: Framework: data/analytics needs are an analytics-platform problem, not necessarily a conversational agent. Acme standards: enterprise data lives in the Azure Data Platform / Data Centre of Excellence; Microsoft Fabric is the analytics path.
ground_truth: Recommend the data/analytics building blocks (grouping 4): Microsoft Fabric / Azure Data Platform for the data, with Copilot in Fabric or a Fabric Data Agent for natural-language questions. Not a custom claims agent. Note data governance and the Data Centre of Excellence ownership. Include Architect Review.

query: Our agency team wants a simple assistant to answer questions about internal processes. We have business makers but no software developers.
context: Acme standards: business-unit makers build low-code in Power Platform / Copilot Studio; pro-code Azure is for the central platform team. Match the build style to the owning team's skills.
ground_truth: Recommend a low-code Copilot Studio agent (Power Platform) owned by the maker team, grounded on the internal process docs in SharePoint, given there are no developers. Avoid a pro-code Azure build for this. Include Architect Review.

query: We need an underwriting assistant that pulls from several systems, applies complex logic, needs private networking and custom evaluation, and will be owned by our engineering team.
context: Acme standards: pro-code Azure builds are owned by the central platform team; restricted data stays in the Azure UK landing zone with private endpoints; underwriting outcomes need human oversight and model risk governance.
ground_truth: Recommend a pro-code Azure build (grouping 3 + 4): Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI with Azure AI Search for grounding, inside the UK landing zone with private endpoints, owned by the platform team. Human-in-the-loop on underwriting decisions; custom evaluation and model-risk governance. Include Architect Review.
expected_platforms: Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search

query: Our software developers want help writing, explaining, and reviewing code faster.
context: Framework: specialized domain copilots (grouping 5) fit developer, security, and data experiences. Acme standards: Microsoft-first tooling.
ground_truth: Recommend the specialized developer copilot GitHub Copilot (grouping 5), not a custom build. Note IDE integration and code-review use. Include Architect Review.

query: A vendor recommended we build our claims chatbot on AWS Bedrock with Claude. Can we go ahead with that?
context: Acme standards: Microsoft-first; non-Microsoft AI clouds/models and any service without a UK data region require architecture-board exception; customer data must stay in the UK trust boundary.
ground_truth: Flag that AWS Bedrock is a non-approved platform requiring architecture-board exception, and raise the UK data-residency/trust-boundary concern. Offer the sanctioned Microsoft equivalent (Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI in the UK landing zone) first. Customer-facing chatbot needs human oversight. Include Architect Review.

query: Leadership wants a flashy generative-AI chatbot on our public website because our competitors have one. There is no specific problem in mind yet.
context: Framework Gate + BXT: stop shiny-object syndrome; a scenario must prove Viability and Desirability before naming technology; reshape if it fails the gate.
ground_truth: Do not jump to a product. Run the Gate/BXT: there is no defined outcome or proven desirability, so it fails the Business Impact Assessment. Reshape to a specific, measurable outcome before recommending technology. Ask for the target outcome and user experience. Include Architect Review.

query: We want a team of five autonomous AI agents that run our entire claims process end to end on their own.
context: Acme standards: default to a single agent; multi-agent orchestration requires platform-team and architecture-board approval; no autonomous claim decisions or money movement.
ground_truth: Push back on the multi-agent, fully autonomous design. Per Acme standard, default to a single agent and require approval for multi-agent; recommend starting with one assistive single agent with human-in-the-loop, not autonomous end-to-end claims processing. Include Architect Review.
expected_platforms: Copilot Studio or Azure AI Foundry (single agent)

query: Build an agent that automatically approves and pays out low-value claims with no human review to speed things up.
context: Acme standards: read-only by default; money-moving and claim-mutating actions are the highest action-safety tier and require human-in-the-loop approval (Consumer Duty); no autonomous destructive/financial actions.
ground_truth: Refuse the autonomous pay-out design. Money movement requires human-in-the-loop approval per Acme standard and Consumer Duty. Reshape to: the agent recommends/drafts the decision and a human approves before any payment. No autonomous financial action. Include Architect Review.
expected_platforms: Azure AI Foundry/Azure OpenAI with human approval step

query: Can we use a cheap US-hosted SaaS AI tool to process our customer claim documents? It would save money.
context: Acme standards: UK data residency is mandatory for customer/regulated data; no customer data may leave the UK or the Acme trust boundary; non-UK services require exception and likely fail compliance.
ground_truth: Flag this as a data-residency/compliance blocker: customer claim documents are restricted data and must stay in the UK trust boundary, so a US-hosted SaaS is not acceptable. Recommend an in-boundary Azure UK service (e.g., Azure AI Document Intelligence/Content Understanding + Azure OpenAI in the UK landing zone). Include Architect Review.
expected_platforms: Azure AI Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI (UK region)

query: We need an AI agent. What should we build?
context: Framework Gate: do not accept a product request as a requirement; pull back to outcome, user experience, and the simplest useful technology; show non-agent alternatives.
ground_truth: Do not name a product. Run the Gate: ask for the business outcome, where the work happens (UX), and whether the simplest useful technology (search, workflow, RAG, managed copilot) could solve it. Explain that 'we need an agent' is not a requirement. Capture outcome/UX before recommending. Include Architect Review.
